name: HC-12 433 MHz wireless serial module
description: 433.4-473.0 MHz half-duplex wireless serial (UART) link module (Silicon Labs Si4463 radio + STM8S003 MCU, up to 100 mW / 20 dBm, about 1 km line of sight at 5 kbps air rate). Two modules on the same channel, baud and FU mode act as a wireless serial cable. Factory 9600 8N1, channel 001 (433.4 MHz), FU3, +20 dBm. Pull SET low for AT commands. Supply 3.2-5.5 V into the module's LDO; RXD/TXD are 3.3 V TTL with 1k series resistors. Sold as: HC-12 433 MHz wireless serial module (HC-12 V2.x by hc01.com and its clones) with the 5-pin 2.54 mm header VCC, GND, RXD, TXD, SET and a spring antenna, the common module sold by most hobby shops.
eli5: Two of these let your boards send text to each other by radio, up to hundreds of metres apart, like an invisible serial cable.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply 3.2-5.5 V, able to give 200 mA (up to 100 mA while transmitting at 20 dBm). Datasheet: add a 1N4007 in series above 4.5 V for long transmit duty

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: Module's UART input, 3.3 V TTL (1k series, weak pull-up). Wire to the microcontroller's TX; use a divider from a 5 V board

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: Module's UART output, 3.3 V TTL (1k series). Wire to the microcontroller's RX

pins.name: SET
pins.description: AT command mode when low (internal 10k pull-up to 3.3 V). Driven by a GPIO so the driver can read and change settings; held high for normal radio use

buildNotes: You need two HC-12s (one per board). Both must use the same channel, baud and FU mode; factory settings already match (CH001, 9600 8N1, FU3).
Cross the serial lines: module TXD to the board's RX, module RXD to the board's TX. RXD/TXD are 3.3 V TTL; from a 5 V Arduino put a 1k/2k divider on RXD.
Power from 3.3 V or 5 V; the supply must handle about 100 mA bursts while transmitting. Add 10-100 uF across VCC/GND near the module if it resets while sending.
Solder the spring antenna (or use the IPEX socket). Without an antenna range drops to a few metres and the radio can be stressed.

AT mode: pull SET low, wait 40 ms, send commands with no line ending (replies end in CRLF). Release SET and wait 80 ms before sending data; wait 200 ms before entering AT mode again. New settings apply after leaving AT mode and survive power-off.

In FU3 the air rate follows the UART baud: 1200-2400 baud -> 5 kbps (longest range), 4800-9600 -> 15 kbps, 19200-38400 -> 58 kbps, 57600-115200 -> 236 kbps. Leave five channels between neighbouring links.

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from hc12 import HC12

u = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RXD}), rx=Pin({TXD}))
radio = HC12(u, Pin({SET}, Pin.OUT, value=1))
try:
    radio.ping()
    print('HC-12 channel %d, %d baud, FU%d, %d dBm' % (radio.channel(), radio.baud(), radio.mode(), radio.power_dbm()))
except OSError as e:
    print(e)
radio.exit_at()  # SET high: transparent mode
print('Listening')
while True:
    line = radio.readline()
    if line:
        print('RECEIVED %s' % line)
        radio.write(b'ack ' + line.encode() + b'\r\n')
    time.sleep_ms(20)

test.title: Reads its settings over AT, then prints what the other HC-12 sends
